posts.title: What to Prepare Before You Hire an Architect
posts.excerpt: A short checklist that makes the first design conversation more productive — even if the project is still only an idea.
body: You do not need a finished brief before speaking with an architect. You do, however, get a better first conversation when you can describe the outcome you want, the site you are working with, and the constraints that matter most.

Start with four things: location, approximate scope, target timing and a realistic budget range. If you have a survey, photos, sketches, precedent images or existing drawings, bring them — but do not delay the conversation because those materials are incomplete.
The goal of an early architectural conversation is not to have every answer. It is to identify the right questions, expose major constraints and define the next useful piece of work.

posts.title: Why Buildability and Budget Belong in the Design Conversation
posts.excerpt: Beautiful drawings are only useful when the project can move through pricing, documentation and construction without avoidable surprises.
body: Design quality and cost discipline are not opposites. The strongest projects treat budget, construction logic and spatial ambition as connected design inputs from the beginning.

Early cost feedback helps the team decide where complexity creates real value and where a simpler solution can protect both the budget and the intent. This is especially important before detailed documentation locks expensive decisions in place.
Value engineering works best as a design activity — not as a late-stage exercise in removing features after pricing arrives.

posts.title: The First Questions to Ask Before Masterplanning a Site
posts.excerpt: Before drawing roads, parcels or buildings, understand the forces that decide what the site can realistically become.
body: Masterplanning starts with constraints and opportunity, not with a pretty site plan. Access, topography, drainage, zoning, utilities, market assumptions and phasing can all reshape the development strategy.

The early objective is to discover which variables are fixed and which can be designed around. Once those are visible, density, circulation, open space and building placement become much more informed decisions.
A clear feasibility stage can prevent a development team from spending time refining a concept that conflicts with the realities of the site.

steps.title: Consultation
steps.description: Establishing the core vision, site feasibility, and budget strategy for your custom home or new commercial development.

steps.title: Schematic Design
steps.description: Translating initial ideas into foundational concepts, focusing on massing, site placement, and overall structural scale.

steps.title: 2D Layout
steps.description: Engineering the precise technical floor plans to optimize spatial flow, usability, and municipal code compliance.

steps.title: Basic 3D Model
steps.description: Building an accurate digital representation of the structure to validate the design, coordinate spatial elements, and ensure proper rooflines and scale.

steps.title: Construction Documents (CDs)
steps.description: Drafting the exact, permit-ready technical blueprints and specifications required by the general contractor to build the project perfectly.

steps.title: Strategic Consultation
steps.description: Defining the exact scope of the remodel, budget constraints, and municipal zoning requirements before any physical work begins.

steps.title: Site Survey & Data Capture
steps.description: Deploying precise measuring tools to capture the exact dimensions, structural elements, and existing conditions of the physical site.

steps.title: As-Built Documentation
steps.description: Drafting highly accurate 2D floor plans and existing-condition data to serve as the flawless baseline for your renovation.

steps.title: Proposed Design & Demolition Plans
steps.description: Developing the new layout, indicating exactly what structural elements will be removed, and mapping the optimized spatial flow.

steps.title: Basic 3D Model
steps.description: Building a clean, functional digital model of the newly proposed layout to validate the design and spatial flow before final engineering.

steps.title: Construction Documents & Permitting
steps.description: Finalizing the technical blueprints and submitting the complete drawing set to the city for expedited permit approval.

steps.title: Asset Collection
steps.description: We take your finalized 2D blueprints, sketches, or CAD files and review the specific aesthetic goals for your marketing or investor pitch.

steps.title: Geometry & "Clay" Modeling
steps.description: Building the foundational 3D geometry of the space without textures, allowing you to approve the camera angles, lighting, and spatial proportions.

steps.title: Material & Texture Integration
steps.description: Applying lifelike materials, landscaping, interior furnishings, and accurate lighting scenarios to bring the digital twin to life.

steps.title: Client Review & Refinement
steps.description: You review the high-resolution drafts to ensure the finishes, mood, and branding perfectly match your vision.

steps.title: Final Photorealistic Delivery
steps.description: Handing over the final, market-ready exterior renders, interior views, and interactive virtual walkthroughs used to secure funding and pre-sales.
